distribution.title: The data are collected and generated to test the project’s central hypothesis that predator stress during larval development causes metabolic reprogramming and related behavioural and memory changes in Drosophila melanogaster, and that these effects differ among fast-, intermediate-, and slow-developing life-history groups. The dataset will support biochemical, physiological and behavioural comparisons between predator-exposed and control flies, as well as analyses of stress resistance, locomotion, learning, and short-/long-term memory for scientific publications, student theses, and project dissemination.

dmp.description: This DMP outlines how data from the  LZP FLPP project # lzp-2024/1-0437  (behavioural assays and biochemical/physiological measurements in Drosophila melanogaster) will be managed throughout the data life cycle—collection, documentation, secure storage/backup, and sharing of publishable datasets via repositories (e.g., Zenodo/Dryad) to support reproducibility and compliance.

project.description: Natural chronic stress has been proposed as a risk factor for the development of metabolic disorders. Predation risk has been recently shown to cause diabetes-like biochemical and behavioral phenotypes in insects with complete metamorphosis and fast larval development. Fast,intermediate, and slow developmental speeds represent different life history strategies of the common fruit fly (Drosophila melanogaster) in a bet-hedging strategy. These life histories may differ in their physiological costs and stress reactivity. In this project, we will test if fruit flies may develop a diabeteslike biochemical and behavioral phenotype when developing at fast, intermediate, or slow speeds. We also will test how learning and memory retention are linked with life history strategies. The project's expected results will make D. melanogaster a better model for studying developmental stress and metabolic disorders.
